concerns.location: plan.md:section 1 (Summary) / research.md:section 2 (Conflict generation) – lines describing deterministic antonym‑based conflict injection and the graph parser’s antonym‑based contradiction detection
concerns.text: The evaluation uses a conflict set generated by a deterministic antonym‑injection rule (research.md) and a graph parser that detects contradictions using the same antonym dictionary. Because the predictor (graph‑augmented verifier) is built to recognise exactly the pattern used to create the test conflicts, the validation is not independent – it risks a circular/tautological confirmation that the graph helps, when in fact the graph is simply mirroring the synthetic conflict generation rule. The robustness hold‑out (back‑translation) still preserves the original antonymic contradictions, so it does not break this dependency. This undermines the scientific claim that the symbolic layer generalises to real‑world conflicting instructions.
